main_body: Stone forge: a grey chimney hood on top and a brick hearth below with a fire opening and a light ledge strip, all drawn face-on.
top_band: None. The middle column starts with a dark outline at row 0, then a flat grey panel at rows 1-3 and a light 2px strip at rows 4-5. This is the front face of the hood, not a horizontal surface.
evidence: The hood is a vertical grey panel with a thin light strip, so no top surface is visible from above. The fire opening (rows 18-24) is a flat front-view slot with flames painted in it, and the ledge at rows 25-26 is a 1-2px light line. No horizontal surface reads as a top, so this is a front elevation with only a rim.

style.evidence: The fire has a good warm ramp, but the stone and hood use only about 3-4 grey steps. The hood panel and the checker-dither corners are large flat or regular fills with little per-stone shading or grain. The outline is a dark neutral blue-grey that leans only slightly toward the material. Beside the Beodeul houses, which have scalloped tiles, plaster speckle and shaded stones, the forge looks thinner and flatter. Most tiles carry only a few colours, apart from the fire tiles.
